system_prompt_style.evidence_quote: Each LLM stage in the workflow uses a modular prompt template with the same general organization, while the content of each section is specialized to the task at hand.
system_prompt_style.note: Stage-specific templates with inputs (FUT, logs, retrieved context); arguably dynamically_composed when VDB context is injected.

env_context_strategy.evidence_quote: a VDB implemented using Chroma stores and retrieves existing functions (knowledge base), existing UTs (ground truth), and reusable test doubles (libraries).
env_context_strategy.note: VDB retrieval is a configuration option (LCA-only disables it); the model does not navigate with tools.

observation_format.evidence_quote: Fixes problems found by the build or test run (compile errors, link errors, test run issues, or coverage gaps) using small edits.
observation_format.note: Build logs, dispatcher output and LCOV hit/miss maps are fed as text.

tool_call_format.evidence_quote: Each LLM step must return its output in a fixed format, so the workflow can reliably read and apply it. In our implementation, we use output schemas for:
tool_call_format.note: Structured output schemas via LangChain; the exact mechanism is not stated. This is closer to fixed-pipeline outputs than to tool calls.

tool_count.note: No tools are exposed to the model; the LLM stages are nodes in a graph.

edit_primitive.evidence_quote: Repair/refinement edits: returns small, specific edits to apply when fixing build/test failures or improving coverage.
edit_primitive.note: The drafting stage emits full ut_c/ut_h files; the repair stage emits small edits whose format is unspecified.

loop_primitives.evidence_quote: The automated workflow is implemented as a state graph consisting of 11 steps (Figure 5).
loop_primitives.note: A LangGraph pipeline with a compile/dispatch/resolve repair loop.

planning_granularity.evidence_quote: Steps: This section provides the stage-by-stage procedure the model should follow.

multi_agent_topology.evidence_quote: a workflow using multiple specialized LLM agents: some draft the initial UT files, others fix build issues using compiler/linker logs

delegation_mechanism.evidence_quote: LangGraph StateGraphhandles the workflow orchestration as a set of steps (nodes) with iterative loops
delegation_mechanism.note: Fixed hand-off between graph nodes through shared state.

human_in_loop.evidence_quote: In interactive mode, a user may review intermediate outputs and provide feedback; in non-interactive mode, execution is fully automated and governed by predefined stopping criteria.
human_in_loop.note: Feedback happens at the break_point_2 iteration gate; which mode is the default is not stated.

short_term_state.evidence_quote: load— Initializes workflow state and validates inputs.

long_term_memory.evidence_quote: it maintains three Chroma collections and issues one targeted query per collection:
long_term_memory.note: The collections are a prebuilt project index rather than memory from past runs.

self_verification.evidence_quote: compile_node— Builds the UT with EDK II and saves the compiler/linker output
self_verification.note: Adds a harness-run build, dispatch and LCOV coverage step; prompts contain a Validation section.

retry_policy.evidence_quote: The system maintains a structured loop that continues until either a coverage threshold is reached or a maximum number of iterations is exceeded.
retry_policy.note: Default target is 90% coverage, with a limit of 10 iterations.

termination_condition.evidence_quote: The workflow stops when any of the following happens: (i) the non-interactive coverage target is reached (90% or above by default), (ii) coverage stops improving under break_point_2, or (iii) the workflow reaches its set iteration limit.

cost_controls.evidence_quote: The workflow was instantiated with three commercially available LLMs selected to balance capability and computational cost.
cost_controls.note: Models are assigned per stage by task.

execution_isolation.evidence_quote: All experiments ran on a Windows machine with the EDK II build environment installed

tracing.evidence_quote: dispatch_node — Runs the UT, saves the run logs, and generates coverage using LCOV

eval_hooks.note: The harness code is not public.

guardrails.evidence_quote: If a symbol is on the list, the workflow avoids generating a new definition for it.

target_domain.evidence_quote: This study introduces an automated UT authoring workflow for the Open-Source Silicon Initialization Library (openSIL) firmware codebase

open_source.evidence_quote: Additional code used in this work cannot be made publicly available due to legal and contractual restrictions
open_source.note: Only the target codebase openSIL is MIT-licensed; the harness is closed.

model_agnostic.evidence_quote: the LLM interactions are managed throughLangChain ChatOpenAI.

primary_artifact.evidence_quote: A pseudocode representation of the workflow pipeline developed in this study is provided as Supplementary Material
primary_artifact.note: The linked repo is the target codebase, not the harness.

first_release_date.note: Paper v2 is dated 21 Jun 2026; the v1 date is not given.

pinned_version.note: No harness repo exists. The provided repo, openSIL genoa_poc@632b97619c45, is the evaluation target (the paper used phoenix_poc), not the harness.

stars.note: The star count is for the openSIL firmware repo, not a harness repo. The count's date is not stated; the date shown is the commit date.
